issue.title: MySQL op.create_index() generates invalid SQL for descending index

labels.name: external SQLAlchemy issues
labels.description: the issue is in SQLAlchemy, not here in alembic

repository.name: alembic
repository.description: A database migrations tool for SQLAlchemy.

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
When creating a descending index with op.create_index and sa.text in columns arg it generates invalid SQL statement such as 
```SQL
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ix_created_at ON test ((created_at desc))
```

**Expected behavior**
The generated SQL statement is correct

**To Reproduce**
I'm able to reproduce the problem reliably with this migration
```py
"""test

Revision ID: aeeacd6ac99d
Create Date: 2020-12-26 11:13:02.177139

"""
from alembic import op
import sqlalchemy as sa


# revision identifiers, used by Alembic.
revision = 'aeeacd6ac99d'
branch_labels = None
depends_on = None


def upgrade():
    op.create_table('test',
                    sa.Column('id', sa.Integer, nullable=False),
                    sa.Column('status', sa.String(length=50), nullable=False),
                    sa.Column('created_at', sa.DateTime(), nullable=False),
                    sa.Column('updated_at', sa.DateTime(), nullable=False),
                    sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint('id')
                    )
    op.create_index('ix_created_at', 'test', [sa.text('created_at desc')], unique=True)


def downgrade():
    pass

```

body:
note that MySQL requires the unusual double parenthesis for most functional expressions:

```
        self.assert_compile(
            schema.CreateIndex(Index("bar", t1.c.x > 5)),
            "CREATE INDEX bar ON foo ((x > 5))",
        )
        self.assert_compile(
            schema.CreateIndex(idx1),
            "CREATE INDEX test_idx1 ON testtbl ((x + y))",
        )
        self.assert_compile(
            schema.CreateIndex(idx2),
            "CREATE INDEX test_idx2 ON testtbl (x, (x + y), (y - x))",
        )

```

this was added in 1.3 for #5462 so the text case here is a regression we can fix in the 1.3 series

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**narrow the check for double-paren exprs in mysql create_index** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2434

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**narrow the check for double-paren exprs in mysql create_index** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2435

> unclear if this is generalized to other dialects yet

It appears not, at least not for mssql:

``` python
engine = sa.create_engine(
    connection_uri,
    future=True,
    echo=True,
)
print(engine.dialect.name)  # mssql

m = sa.MetaData()

tbl = sa.Table(
    "testtbl",
    m,
    sa.Column("data", sa.String(255)),
    sa.Column("created_at", sa.DateTime),
)
idx = sa.Index("test_idx1", sa.text("created_at desc"), _table=tbl)
m.drop_all(engine, checkfirst=True)
m.create_all(engine)
"""SQL rendered:
CREATE TABLE testtbl (
	data VARCHAR(255) NULL, 
	created_at DATETIME NULL
)
CREATE INDEX test_idx1 ON testtbl (created_at desc)
"""
```
